_meta.indication: Treatment of adults and pediatric patients aged 16 years and older with metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma not eligible for complete resection; approved under accelerated approval based on ORR and DOR.

pivotal_trials.population: Patients with histologically confirmed, metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma required to have INI1 loss and an ECOG performance status of 0-2
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Confirmed overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1 by blinded independent central review, and duration of response (DOR)
pivotal_trials.n: 62 patients in Cohort 5 (with an additional 44 in Cohort 6)
pivotal_trials.result: Cohort 5 ORR 15% (95% CI: 7%, 26%); Complete Response 1.6%, Partial Response 13%; 67% of responses had duration ≥ 6 months. Pooled Cohorts 5+6 ORR 13% (95% CI: 7, 21).

key_safety: Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions were pain (52%), fatigue (47%), nausea (36%), decreased appetite (26%), vomiting (24%), and constipation (21%). Most serious risk is secondary malignancies (MDS/AML in 0.6% of 668 adults; one pediatric T-LBL).
target_moa: First-in-class, orally administered small molecule inhibitor of the methyltransferase EZH2 (enhancer of zeste homolog 2), the catalytic subunit of PRC2 that methylates lysine 27 of histone H3 leading to transcriptional repression.
companion_dx_detail: The Applicant did not develop a companion diagnostic for tazemetostat; INI1 status was determined by local tests without a required companion diagnostic.

advisory_committee.vote: ODAC met December 18, 2019 and voted unanimously 11-0 that the demonstrated benefit of tazemetostat outweighs the risks in the proposed indication.

surrogate_endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) and duration of response (DOR); ORR is an intermediate endpoint.

citations.quote: This indication is approved under accelerated approval based on overall response rate and duration of response [see *Clinical Studies (14)*]. Continued approval for this indication may be contingent upon verification and description of clinical benefit in a confirmatory trial(s).

confirmatory_requirement.text: Submit the final results from a confirmatory randomized trial in patients with epithelioid sarcoma to confirm clinical benefit (PMR 3787-1).

citations.quote: 3787-1 Submit the final results from a confirmatory randomized trial in patients with epithelioid sarcoma to confirm clinical benefit and provide additional efficacy data that may inform product labeling for tazemetostat.

orphan_indication.text: TAZVERIK has an orphan drug designation for this indication (epithelioid sarcoma); the applicant was therefore exempt from the PREA pediatric assessment requirement.

citations.quote: Because this drug product for this indication has an orphan drug designation, you are exempt from this requirement.

basis.text: The application was reviewed as Priority.

summary.text: Tazemetostat, a new molecular entity, received Priority Review and accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314 subpart H based on ORR and DOR from single-arm Cohort 5 of Study EZH-202, with a required confirmatory randomized trial to verify clinical benefit; ODAC voted 11-0 in favor.

citations.quote: On May 23, 2019, Epizyme submitted NDA 211723 under 21 CFR 314.50 and section 505 (b)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, seeking accelerated approval of tazemetostat tablets (200 mg) for the following proposed indication:
It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling.

requirement.text: 3787-1: Submit final results from a confirmatory randomized trial in patients with epithelioid sarcoma to confirm clinical benefit.

citations.quote: 3787-1 Submit the final results from a confirmatory randomized trial in patients with epithelioid sarcoma to confirm clinical benefit and provide additional efficacy data that may inform product labeling for tazemetostat.

requirement.text: 3787-2: Submit final report and datasets for the final analysis of ORR and DOR for clinical trial EZH-202.

citations.quote: 3787-2 Submit the final report and datasets for the final analysis of overall response rate and duration of response for clinical trial EZH-202 titled, “A Phase II, Multicenter Study of the EZH2 Inhibitor Tazemetostat in Adult Subjects With INI1-Negative Tumors or Relapsed/Refractory Synovial Sarcoma” to verify and confirm clinical benefit of tazemetostat, that may inform product labeling. An additional 25 patients from Cohort 6 beyond those included in the original NDA submission will be evaluated and all responding patients will be followed for at least 12 months from the onset of response.

requirement.text: 3787-3: Conduct cumulative, integrated safety analyses after 5 and 10 years of follow-up to characterize the risk of AML, MDS, T-lymphoblastic lymphoma, and other secondary malignancies.

citations.quote: 3787-3 Conduct cumulative, integrated safety analyses after 5 and 10 years of follow-up from an adequate number of patients enrolled in clinical trials to characterize the risk of acute myeloid leukemia, myelodysplastic syndrome, T-lymphoblastic lymphoma, and other secondary malignancies in patients receiving TAZVERIK; include incidence rates, time to onset, predisposing factors, and outcomes. These safety evaluations will be adequate to inform labeling of patient populations at highest risk and to provide evidence-based monitoring recommendations.

requirement.text: 3787-4: Conduct a pharmacokinetic and safety study in cancer patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.

citations.quote: 3787-4 Conduct a pharmacokinetic and safety study in cancer patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment investigating the effects of hepatic impairment (based on the NCI Organ Dysfunction Working Group (ODWG) criteria) on the repeat dose pharmacokinetics of tazemetostat compared to cancer patients with normal hepatic function. This study will assess the magnitude of increased tazemetostat exposure and determine appropriate dosing recommendations of tazemetostat for patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment.

requirement.text: 3787-5: Conduct a cross-over study investigating the effects of itraconazole, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, on the repeat dose PK of tazemetostat.

citations.quote: 3787-5 Conduct a cross-over study in patients with cancer investigating the effects of itraconazole, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, on the repeat dose pharmacokinetics of tazemetostat to assess the magnitude of increased tazemetostat exposure and to determine appropriate dosing recommendations for tazemetostat when it is administered concomitantly with strong CYP3A inhibitors.

requirement.text: 3787-6: Conduct a cross-over study investigating the effects of rifampin, a strong CYP3A inducer, on the repeat dose PK of tazemetostat.
